data.name: January
data.long_meaning: January is derived from the Latin word 'ianuarius', which is related to 'janua', meaning 'door'. January was named after the Roman god Janus, who is the god of beginnings, gates, doors, and endings. In many cultures, January represents a time of new beginnings and fresh starts.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of new beginnings and the door to opportunities.

in_hebrew.name: ינואר
in_hebrew.meaning: ראש השנה החדשה, ינואר, חודש ראשון
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ינואר הוא השם העברי לחודש הראשון בשנה הגרגוריאנית, מקורו בשם הרומי יאנוארוס, שנתן השם לחודש הראשון בשנה, על שם האל הרומי יאנוס, אל הדלתות, ההתחלות והסופים, נוצרים רבים בוחרים לתת שם זה לילדיהם הנולדים בחודש ינואר, כהוקרה לשנה החדשה

in_greek.name: Ιανουάριος
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιανουάριος είναι ο πρώτος μήνας του έτους στο Γρηγοριανό ημερολόγιο, πήρε το όνομά του από τον Ρωμαϊκό θεό Ιανό, που ήταν ο θεός των θυρών, των αρχών και των τελειών, οι Χριστιανοί συχνά επιλέγουν να ονομάσουν τα παιδιά τους Ιανουάριος, ως φόρο τιμής στον νέο χρόνο

in_latin.name: Ianuarius
in_latin.long_meaning: Ianuarius est nomen Latinum mensis primi anni, ab Ianuario, deo Romanorum ianuae, principiorum et finium, dictus, Christiani saepe hoc nomen infantibus suis qui mense Ianuario nati sunt, imponentes, ut novum annum honorerent

in_english.name: January
in_english.meaning: First month of the year, derived from Roman god Janus
in_english.long_meaning: January is the first month of the year in the Gregorian calendar, derived from the Roman god Janus, who was the god of doors, beginnings, and endings, Christians often choose to name their children January, as a tribute to the new year, symbolizing new beginnings and fresh starts

data.cultural_impact: January is considered the first month of the year in the Gregorian calendar. It is a time of new beginnings and fresh starts, often marked by resolutions and goals. Many cultures celebrate this month with festivals and celebrations, such as New Year's Day, which is celebrated on January 1st.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, January is a time to reflect on the previous year and look forward to the new one with hope and anticipation. It is a reminder of God's faithful provision and goodness, as well as an opportunity to seek His guidance and strength in the new year. It is also a time to remember the birth of Jesus, who is the door to salvation and the source of new life. (John 10:9)
